title: Stable-channel image mirroring and artifact contract for CUDA/driver stacks
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Establish a stable-channel image mirroring workflow and a machine-readable artifact contract for CUDA and driver stacks to guarantee predictable upgrades across Dedicated and Private deployments. The aim is to enable a single trusted 'stable' registry mirror per region that contains signed images, SBOMs, and a compatibility contract describing which driver/CUDA/kernel ABI combinations are validated for each runtime image.
background: We currently surface images and SBOMs, but there is no canonical contract describing acceptable combinations of GPU drivers, CUDA minor versions, and kernel ABI expectations. This causes coordination friction during rollouts and forces ad-hoc pinning for customers on Dedicated/Private. Mirroring to a stable channel per region will allow safe roll-forward paths and quick rollback by flipping mirror pointers, while the artifact contract will be used by the upgrade assistant and CI presubmits to validate compatibility.
goals: 1) Define an artifact contract schema that records tested driver/CUDA/kernel ABI tuples and the validated model of quantization/ops for a given runtime image. 2) Implement automatic mirroring from CI-build artifacts into region-stable registries with signature verification and SBOM binding. 3) Wire the upgrade-assistant to consult the contract and the stable mirror when proposing upgrades or fallbacks to customers.
acceptance_criteria: A JSON artifact contract exists and is generated by the image build pipeline for every runtime image
Stable-channel mirrors exist for us-west1 and eu-west1 with signed image manifests and associated SBOMs
Upgrade assistant and dedicated autoscaler consult the contract and will refuse an automatic upgrade if contract compatibility is unsatisfied
Documentation (operator runbook and public KB) describing how to pin or opt out of stable-channel mirroring
E2E test that simulates a canary rollback via mirror pointer switch is added to release CI
implementation_steps: Design contract schema: fields for image_digest, sbom_digest, signed_at, tested_driver_versions, tested_cuda_versions, kernel_abi_range, validated_ops_list, provenance_links
Prototype generator in image-build CI to emit contract JSON and sign with release KMS key
Add mirror-promotion job that pushes signed manifest+sbom+contract to stable registry per region and publishes a pointer tag (e.g., stable-2025-03)
Modify release controller to support mirror pointer flips as atomic roll-forward/rollback operation
Add contract validator library used by upgrade-assistant and presubmit CI to validate a target host's driver/kernel against the contract
Update operator runbooks and Console UI to show contract details on image pages

test_plan: Unit tests for contract generator and schema validation
Integration test: build image -> generate contract -> sign -> promote to stable mirror -> pull from stable mirror and verify signature and SBOM binding
Presubmit: validate that contract validator rejects mismatched kernel ABI/driver combos
E2E CI: simulate regional mirror outage and verify automatic fallback to global mirror pointer
rollout_gates: Gate 1: Contract schema reviewed and approved by Release, Security, and Platform
Gate 2: Mirror promotion pipeline successfully executed in staging for 2 consecutive runs
Gate 3: Upgrade assistant integration validated against 3 Dedicated staging clusters
Gate 4: Security scan of signed artifacts passes (no secret leakage in SBOMs)
rollback_plan: If a promoted stable image shows regressions, flip the region stable pointer to previous stable tag within 15 minutes
Notify on-call release-engineer and create incident record; keep faulty image in quarantined registry path
If pointer flip doesn't resolve, run host-level rollback playbook to revert nodes to previously pinned image and drivers
Postmortem within 72 hours and mark contract/build as invalidated with audit trail
risks: Incompatible kernel ABI ranges for some customer kernels; mitigated by conservative kernel_abi_range and explicit opt-out
Mirror promotion could become a single point of mistake; mitigate via signed manifests and required code review for promotion PRs
SBOM sensitivity exposing internal package names; mitigate by redaction rules and security review
Operator confusion over 'stable' semantics; mitigate with clear docs and Console UX showing exact validated tuples
notes: This work is complementary to ENG-14001 (image rotation sync) but focuses on the contract and stable pointer semantics rather than bulk rotation
We should coordinate with Dedicated onboarding to ensure the operator can opt into region mirrors or host a local mirror
Consider exposing a lightweight API endpoint for customers to query the contract and get driver/CUDA compatibility advice
